raw_evidence.quote: `gen-sqlddl` emits foreign keys to inherited injected identifiers instead of a class's direct identifier
the generated FK target was incorrectly pointing to Person.id when the Person table's direct identifier was name
the issue recommends that for generated relational tables, PK/FK resolution should prefer the class's direct identifier/key attribute rather than an inherited identifier
annotations schema does not support multiple values for an annotation key: need an Any type? · Issue #296 · linkml/linkml
raw_evidence.locator: search result title, unrelated LinkML issue surfaced by the same query batch (annotations, not the ten advanced constructs) — recorded for completeness, not used as evidence for any construct classification

composite_pk_and_fk_generation_reliabili.rationale: This issue is direct primary-source contrary evidence that even LinkML's SINGULAR-identifier foreign-key generation logic (the simpler case than any composite key) has had a real, reported defect in FK target resolution when identifiers are inherited. Combined with the metamodel finding that LinkML caps a class at one identifier/key slot (source-linkml-metamodel.json), this issue reinforces that composite-identity FK generation is not a mature, battle-tested path in LinkML's SQL DDL generator — it strengthens rather than contradicts the 'expressible-only-via-workaround' classification recorded for composite primary keys.

self_referencing_fk_gap_search.rationale: No open issue was found via this search method describing a limitation specific to multiple self-referencing foreign keys on one class. This is recorded as an explicit non-finding: the search did not surface evidence either confirming a gap or ruling one out, which leaves the metamodel-level 'expressible' classification (source-linkml-metamodel.json, based on the general range mechanism) unopposed but also not independently corroborated by a real-world issue report.

multi_schema_gap_search.rationale: No open issue was found describing a feature request or limitation for mapping one LinkML schema's classes to multiple distinct database schemas within one physical database. This absence is consistent with (does not contradict) the metamodel-record finding that the SQL DDL generator's documented algorithm is one-LinkML-schema-to-one-DB-schema, but it is also possible relevant discussion exists under different terminology not captured by this search.
